belief: Every decision has one right answer, and I must find it.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that every decision has one right answer that you must find, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Teaching that God has a specific choice for everything, down to what you eat. Perfectionism and fear of mistakes. Anxiety that turns small choices into crises. A home where mistakes were punished harshly. Comparing yourself with people who seem certain about everything.
teaches: Some decisions are clearly right or wrong because Scripture speaks to them. But many choices are about freedom within God’s good boundaries. Paul says whatever you eat or drink, do it all to the glory of God. Believers can come to different conclusions on some matters, each fully convinced in their own mind. God calls us to freedom, to serve one another in love, and to commit our works to Him. In many decisions, there are several good options.
self_statements: There’s only one right choice, and I have to find it.
If I choose wrong, God will be displeased.
I can’t decide until I’m sure it’s the perfect choice.
Other people always know the right answer.
errors: Believing every choice must be the perfect one.
Believing there is only one right answer and everything else is wrong.
Treating small decisions as if they had huge consequences.
questions: Does Scripture speak directly to this decision?
What does 1 Corinthians 10:31 say about everyday choices?
Could there be more than one good option here?
What does Romans 14:5 say about personal convictions?
Am I using freedom to glorify God and serve others?
What is the cost of endlessly searching for the perfect answer?
What would happen if I chose a good option and moved on?
truth: Not every decision has only one right answer. When Scripture is clear, I follow it. In many choices, God gives me freedom to choose among good options. I can commit my plans to the Lord, do everything for His glory, serve others in love, and move forward without fear.
hw_questions: Does Scripture speak directly to this?
Could there be several good options?
Am I using freedom for God and others?
What if I chose a good option and moved on?
hw_truths: Many decisions have more than one good option.
I can do everything to the glory of God.
God gives me freedom within His good boundaries.
I can commit my plans to the Lord.
I don’t have to find the perfect choice.
I can decide and move forward in peace.
log: Each day, write one decision I made, why it was a good option, and that I didn’t second-guess it.
name_example: Sarah can commit her works to the LORD, and her plans will be achieved.
actions: For your next small decision, set a two-minute limit,
choose a good option, and move on.
Write down a past decision you agonized over,
and write what Paul says about freedom and conviction.
tracker: One decision I made without second-guessing
prayer: Father, thank You for the freedom You give me within Your good boundaries. Help me reject the lie that every decision has one right answer that I must find. Teach me to follow Your Word, commit my plans to You, and choose with peace. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
